Anya (PM): Heads-up — competitor A just announced per-route latency tiers + auto-fallback variants. Customers are pinging us for the same guarantee. Need quick call: parity on controls vs double-down on cost transparency? :thinking:
Mike (Eng): Saw that. Their demo looked like an SLO knob per endpoint. Implementation touches routing and runtime.
Sarah (Sales): A couple of pilots asked for predictable tail latency yesterday. They said 'either a strict SLA or an easy way to trade cost for latency.'
Ethan (Director): Prioritize by revenue signal. Which customers are blocked today? Sarah, any names?
Sarah (Sales): Two mid-market customers and one startup on Dedicated. Will share emails after this thread.
Anya (PM): Proposal: ship an MVP parity path that exposes per-route "latency tier" with 3 presets (fast, balanced, cheap) + automatic fallback to next tier when capacity constrained. Then follow with Improve UX: explain cost tradeoffs in Console.
Mike (Eng): Rough infra impact: add routing policy + ability to pin model variant per route. Also need telemetry hooks for latency buckets. Est 3 sprints if we staff a small spike team.
Ethan (Director): Can we scope a smaller spike first: proof that runtime can route to variant X under pressure w/o customer-visible errors?
Mike (Eng): Yes. Spike ticket: validate routing + graceful fallback (no 500s) under saturation. I can do it in 2 weeks with one eng.
Anya (PM): Draft launch criteria (spike -> MVP -> GA). Thoughts?
Anya (PM): ```
- Spike success: simulated load shows fallback on over-capacity, no correctness regressions in >1000 prompt runs.
- MVP: per-route latency tier config + Console dropdown, telemetry for cost/latency per-token, canary with 2 pilot customers.
- GA: docs, SDK flag, SLA language for Dedicated customers, rollout plan.
```
Sarah (Sales): MVP with pilots is critical. We can get two pilots within 4 weeks if MVP is lightweight.
Ethan (Director): Add acceptance metric: <5% error-rate during fallback window and latency percentile targets per tier.
Mike (Eng): Agree. Need product to define exact p50/p95/p99 numbers per tier. Also need to know acceptable cost uplift for "fast" tier.
Anya (PM): Draft numbers for discussion: fast p50 < 80ms, p95 < 250ms; balanced p50 < 120ms p95 < 400ms; cheap p50 < 250ms p95 < 800ms. Cost uplift: fast +40%, balanced +15%, cheap -10% relative to baseline. Open to pushback.
Sarah (Sales): Those look reasonable as starting points. Customers will want more granularity later.
Mike (Eng): Technical constraints: quantized models + batching heuristics may make fast tier expensive. We'll need recommended model variants for each tier in Optimize.
Anya (PM): Action items: @Mike create spike ticket and link perf run by EOD Monday; @Sarah gather pilot names + quick ask doc; @Ethan approve resourcing for a 2-sprint MVP team. ops-bot: create channel?
ops-bot: Created #prod-latency-tiers (private) and a ticket in Jira: PROD-1823. :white_check_mark:
Ethan (Director): Approving 2-sprint band for MVP headcount if spike proves feasible.
Anya (PM): If spike fails, fallback path: document gap and propose a UX-first approach (cost transparency + per-route throttles) to buy time.
Mike (Eng): Noted. I'll post spike plan and initial load test script in the new channel.
Sarah (Sales): I'll queue pilot outreach for next week. Tagging support to ensure SRE on standby for canary. :+1:
Anya (PM): Cool — let's sync Thursday for quick status. :calendar:
